nt: A new scene begins here which may need to be marked in a certain way in your language.

**Amalek** and **Israel** both refer to the nations (people groups) descended from that individual by simply using the name of the ancestor. If your readers would not understand this, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the Amalekites … the Israelites]

**Amalek** and **Israel** are both collective nouns that refer to the nations (people groups) descended from that individual. If your language does not use singular nouns in that way, you can use a different expression. Alternate translation: [the Amalekites … the Israelites]
**Amalek** or the Amalekites are a completely new participant in the story. Use the natural form in your language for introducing a new character.
**Rephidim** was the name of a place in the desert.

nt: God speaks of destroying Amalek as if he were removing people’s memory of Amalek. When a group of people is completely destroyed, there is nothing to remind people about them. If your readers would not understand what this image means in this context, you could use an equivalent metaphor from your culture. Alternatively, you could express the meaning plainly. The Amalekites are referred to by naming their ancestor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Amalekites]

This phrase makes an intentionally broad image and represents all people everywhere. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from all people everywhere]

x.ASV: and he said, Jehovah hath sworn: Jehovah will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
x.Darby: And he said, For the hand is on the throne of Jah; Jehovah will have war with Amalek from generation to generation!
x.KJV: For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
x.YLT: and saith, `Because a hand is on the throne of Jah, war is to Jehovah with Amalek from generation--generation.'

nt: The Hebrew here is very difficult, and there are a variety of opinions regarding the meaning. Questions include: (1) Whose hand is referred to? Amalek’s, Yahweh’s, or Moses’? (2) What is the hand on (or against)? Yahweh’s throne or banner? (3) What is the meaning of the Hebrew preposition meaning on, against, or above? What does that signify? Rebellion, or taking an oath, or holding onto a symbol of power? If there is another translation in your region, it may be best to simply follow the interpretation it gives. Alternate translation: [Because a hand was on the throne of Yah] or [Because a hand was on the banner of Yah]
This phrase has no verbs in Hebrew. You may need to translate the noun **war** as a verb. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will make war with Amalek] or [Yahweh will war against Amalek]
